text: The ceiling comes down, and Borro catches it: a four-metre slab, on his shield and his back.
But his field form has fifty seconds left.
The only way forward is under him. Go, Jaeha shouts.
Dami ducks through, then Woo with Uncle Pyo on his back, then Ho on all fours.
Jaeha's knees buckle with Borro's. He's carrying seventy percent of that slab.
Then two more keystones crack, one ahead and one behind, and the cracks race across the arches.
Jaeha reads the roof. Every crack starts at a keystone. Hold the keystones, and the arches hold themselves.
Three keystones on his blood-spotted page. One each.
Nib takes one, Lyra the other. Hold the keystone, not the roof. Lyra is an archer, not a pillar!
Tonight, Jaeha says through the blood, everybody is a pillar.
He calls them both into field form, five minutes each. Borro has thirty-eight seconds.
Nib braces his back against one keystone. Lyra braces both palms against the other.
Then a red window. Carry times three, limit two. The Operator's body will bear the excess.
His body, Jaeha thinks. His people. Carry.
Three threads pour into him, and he drops to his knees. Carry load: one hundred and eighty percent. Overload.
The edges of his sight go grey. Blood drips onto the steel between his hands.
Moon Ahin raises her baton. Ten and ten, under the arches. Take the weight off his people.
Twenty husks press up on the stone, the cracks stop, and his load drops to one hundred and forty.
Borro's eyes flicker. Three seconds left.
Everyone is through except Jaeha, still at Borro's side. Operator, Borro says. Go.
Borro shoves him through one-handed. The green leaves his eyes, and the slab drives him flat.
Borro is back in rest form, no stronger than an ordinary person, pinned under the slab.
Jaeha crawls back to him. The shell holds, Borro says. Go on, and come back later.
Jaeha grips one of his huge fingers. No. Not later. Everyone comes back now.
On the safe side, the four crew stop and look back.
Uncle Pyo tightens his knee brace and picks up a steel strut. Kanghan hired them as sandbags. Fine. Sandbags can push.
And all four run back toward the slab.
Moon Ahin sends ten husks down off the arches. Don't look at her like that, she says. His rule is catching.
Struts under the edge, husks lifting, Nib and Lyra pushing too. Ho counts it out. One, two, heave!
The slab tips off Borro's shell and slides into the water.
Then everyone collapses in one panting heap round Borro.
Borro lifts his head and looks at the four crew. Thank you.
Uncle Pyo laughs and cries at once. Twenty years, and nobody ever said that to a sandbag.
Ho asks Jaeha, very seriously, if this is normal for him. Usually there's less, Jaeha starts. No. Actually, this is normal.
Ho is horrified. Woo laughs for the first time all night.
Jaeha's legs fold when he tries to stand. Overload, strain severe. Eight minutes forty-seven left.
Moon Ahin holds out her hand. He offered his at the ladder. She's returning it.
His bloody glove takes her white one, and leaves a smear of red.
They climb again, Jaeha on Moon Ahin's arm, Borro limping with Uncle Pyo on his cracked shell.
Carrying three at once is killing him, she says. A little, he admits. Not tonight.
She gives him a sideways look. He's a very strange Number Four.
Nib reports that the boots behind them have stopped. The collapse cut them off. So why does Lyra feel worse?
Jaeha knows why. They don't need to chase. Sora is waiting at the top.
At a junction, the tunnel splits. One branch dark and dry, one following the water toward a faint white light.
Nib says the dry one is safer. Jaeha takes the wet one. The water goes out through the rim. It always knows the way out.
They follow the water. Seven minutes and two seconds.
Dami touches the crack in Borro's shell and asks if it hurts. It hurts him more, says Borro. He takes it.
Dami looks up the walkway at Jaeha, climbing on Moon Ahin's arm.
The walls here are carved with the sea-people's waves, and a small faded giant with a trident watches them pass.
Lyra touches it as she goes by. They'll come back for him. Jaeha said so.
Then the tunnel ends at the foot of a long, steep shaft, white light glowing at the very top.
Uncle Pyo knows this place. He's cleaned that pump room under the rim. It's the only way out.
And at the top, a row of black shields, edge to edge.
Han Sora sits on a pump housing, swinging one boot, twelve troopers kneeling behind their shields, a hundred and twenty metres above them.
Her compass points straight down the shaft. There's only one way out, Operator, and she's sitting on it.
Everyone looks up the long slope at the shields.
Jaeha stands on his own and opens his notebook one more time. A hundred and twenty metres. Twelve carbines. One crossbow.
Six minutes left on the rim.
Twelve carbines take aim down the shaft, and Sora stands up and raises her crossbow.
